Issued at 242 PM EDT Sat Aug 8 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Flow across the northern tier of the CONUS turning more zonal 
upstream...with broad ridge still centered over the Desert SW...and 
various niblets of energy from the Gulf of Alaska trying to connect 
up with the upper low centered over Hudson Bay, but with lobes 
stretching back into central Canada (one such lobe associated with a 
surface trough stretching from Hudson Bay into central Manitoba as 
of 17z). Bermuda high still in place off the Atlantic coast, and we 
remain generally perturbed here in the Upper Great Lakes with 
troughing aloft. Deeper moisture sweeping out of the region attm 
behind a couple weakening cold fronts stretching from IL/IN toward 
James Bay...with skies slowly clearing out and dewpoints slowly 
dropping back into the more comfortable upper 50s/near 60F range. 
This cold front wraps back to the northwest into MT/Saskatchewan as 
a warm/stationary front...with low-level flow through the Plains 
largely orthogonal to this boundary, which also loosely serves as an 
outline of a mid-level EML plume. Between lee-side troughing and 
diurnal heating over the Plains amid this setup, some convective 
activity has developed along the boundary over Nebraska as of 17z. 

Cold front will continue to slide out of the area...but expect 
baroclinic zone to buckle back northward Sunday into Monday...most 
likely stalling out somewhere in the OH Valley or perhaps as far 
north as southern MI, likely through at least midweek, which should 
keep a threat for showers and thunderstorms somewhere across the 
region...most likely to our south, but worth keeping an eye on as 
perturbations move through Canada and enhance confluence and subtle 
upper jet maxima across the region. There are some signals for this 
boundary to shift southward later next week, depending on how 
troughing evolves across eastern Canada late in the period...with 
quite a bit of uncertainty in how things end up going into next 
weekend. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances through the period:
--Tonight/Sunday...lobe of energy across central Canada attm to 
swing southeastward tonight as return flow increases across the 
central Plains...resulting in increased confluence over the Upper 
Great Lakes. While LLJ and deeper moisture should remain well to our 
southwest over the Mid MS Valley tonight...not impossible we could 
get some hints of at least mid-high clouds across parts of the area 
with the northern stream niblet. Think that whatever boundary gets 
dragged in from the north Sunday morning could become a focus for 
redevelopment in the afternoon and into the overnight hours as that 
deeper moisture approaches from the southwest. Left entrance region 
jet dynamics should enhance lifting, with pwats ramping up into the 
1.5-2in range...suggesting we could squeeze a lot of moisture out of 
the air. Plume of weak mid-level stability oozing in further signals 
potential for significant rainfall as it could give us a lot more 
bang for our QPF buck...and we may well be in an area of increased 
threat for training storms going into Sunday night (though not 
impossible these could remain just to our south). Not impossible the 
training storms/MCS idea hang on into Monday with the subtle ridge 
axis just to our west and thickness gradient generally WNW-ESE over 
the region...not impossible this may be what some guidance is 
picking up on as a subtle PV max that slips in from the northwest 
Sunday night, and if this occurs...will need to keep an eye out for 
the focus of heavier rain to shift around from current expectations. 

--Early Next Week... the hits look to keep on coming with signals 
for additional MCS development over the Upper Midwest Monday night 
as well, with another subtle boost to the jet max aloft to enhance 
synoptic lift over this moist, zonal boundary in the region. Most 
likely scenario attm is that the primary boundary and thus, focus 
for convection, will be further south Monday night than Sunday 
night...but can't entirely rule out some concerns for our area, 
pending where upstream convection develops. 

--Midweek... by midweek, will be watching for a lobe of Canadian 
energy to sweep into/by the region (unclear exactly how this unfolds 
attm), which suggests potential for a boost in the upper jet max and 
thus, broad dynamic support along that still-lingering zonal 
boundary in the OH Valley/Great Lakes region. This could be one last 
shot at activity for us, though it remains entirely possible that 
the bulk of the focus for convection will be well south of us by 
this time, and we could remain quiet aside from some diurnal showers 
(could come close to seeing some lake effect rain showers by late 
next week if the coldest solutions verify (850mb temps around 5C) 
and lake surface temps remain stable). 

Overall... current signals point toward the heaviest rain remaining 
to our south/southwest, where there are signals for in excess
